title: Plans per Buyer and per Covered Order — Northloop Protect Plans
content:
**Clause.** Under the Northloop Protect Plans, a buyer may hold any number of protection plans, but each ordered item can be covered by only one plan; a second plan on the same covered order is refused.

There is no maximum number of plans per buyer: the only limit is on the covered item and its covered order, never on the buyer.

## The clause in condition and result

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| The buyer already holds one or more plans, each on a different covered order, and buys a plan for an item on another order | Permitted; the number of plans a buyer holds is not limited |
| A plan already exists on the covered order and a second plan is sought on the same covered order | Refused |

## Basis questions answered

**Does holding several Northloop Protect Plans limit a buyer's next purchase?**
No. A buyer may hold any number of protection plans; the count of plans already held never by itself stops a purchase.

**What is compared when a second plan is sought?**
The covered order of the plan sought is compared with the covered orders of the plans already held. A second plan on the same covered order is refused.

## Hypothetical illustrations

- A buyer holds a Protect 2-Year Extended Warranty on a television from one order and a Protect 3-Year Accident Protection on a laptop from another order, and seeks a plan for a blender from a third order: the number of plans held does not stand in the way.
- A buyer holds a Protect 1-Year Extended Warranty on an order and seeks a Protect 4-Year Accident Protection on that same covered order: the second plan is refused.
